provenance.note: Place name on the river, geocoded to the reach [supplied on this invocation]
Steady upstream discharge the reach is dredged under - the flow that shoals the channel and carries the disturbed material [supplied on this invocation]
Result-writing cadence; unset keeps the steering file's own period [supplied on this invocation]
Modeled reach length downstream of the seed; a longer reach is coarsened under the mesh node budget [supplied on this invocation]
Simulated physical time the dredge campaign runs over; the morphological factor is what makes a short window produce a readable bed change [supplied on this invocation]
Target element edge length the reach is triangulated at; the dredged volume is the sum over the nodes inside the field, so a coarse mesh resolves a narrow fairway badly [supplied on this invocation]
Depth the fairway is dredged TO, under the reference water surface the run opens at - the design draught plus its overdepth [supplied on this invocation]

Depth at which a node is dredged: the bed is worked wherever it sits shallower than this under the reference surface. Equal to design_depth_m keeps the channel exactly at grade; SMALLER than it lets the channel shoal before the dredger returns, and a trigger DEEPER than the grade would mark a node for a cut that is above its own bed [supplied on this invocation]
When the first dredging pass begins, in seconds of the BED's own clock - the run's morphological time, sim_duration_s x morphological_factor [supplied on this invocation]
When the campaign stops, on the same bed clock: no further pass begins after it, and a pass already cutting runs on until it reaches grade [supplied on this invocation]
Maintenance interval on the bed clock: how long after a pass starts the next one begins, if the channel has shoaled past trigger_depth_m again [supplied on this invocation]

How fast the dredger lowers the bed, as metres of bed per second of SOLVER time at a working node - the plant's capacity, not a physical rate. A pass reports its volume only once it has reached grade, so this and the cut it has to make are what decide whether the run sees a completed pass at all [supplied on this invocation]
How fast the spoil is laid into the dump area, as metres of bed per second of solver time at a receiving node; a pass is not finished until its spoil is placed [supplied on this invocation]
Median grain diameter d50 of the bed the channel shoals with - ~200 um fine sand, ~20 um silt (all modeled non-cohesive) [supplied on this invocation]
Depth of the erodible sediment stock the dredger can cut into [supplied on this invocation]
Solve sizing class [declared constant default]
The calendar instant the run's clock starts at, as [year, month, day, hour, minute, second] - the origin every dredge schedule is dated against and the one the deck states [declared scenario default]
Least volume worth moving around a node before it is dredged at all; 0 works every node past the trigger [declared scenario default]
GAIA bed-load law: 1=Meyer-Peter-Mueller, 2=Einstein-Brown, 7=van Rijn [declared scenario default]
Amplifies bed change per hydraulic step so a short campaign yields a readable depth; a speed-up lever, not a rate [declared scenario default]
not supplied; the reach flowline is fetched fresh for the AOI
not supplied; the carrier discharge is read at the MOST RECENT published NWM cycle
not supplied; the reach is solved at Strickler 33.0, which is also the roughness its outflow stage is derived as a normal depth at
not supplied; the coefficient is read as a Strickler one

answer.dredge_report: the volumes are the engine's own report lines, summed over the passes that finished inside the run's clock
answer.discharge_note: Steady upstream discharge the reach is dredged under - the flow that shoals the channel and carries the disturbed material [supplied on this invocation]
answer.mesh_resolution_note: Target element edge length the reach is triangulated at; the dredged volume is the sum over the nodes inside the field, so a coarse mesh resolves a narrow fairway badly [supplied on this invocation]
